name: Surya OCR 2.5

lineage.base_model: Surya 2 (earlier checkpoint of the same line)
lineage.how_derived: single Qwen3.5-style vision-language model for layout, OCR and table reading, trained on diverse document images (card, Training section)

purpose: One small VLM that does layout analysis with reading order, full-page or per-block OCR and table reading as HTML, for document intelligence pipelines; the vendor also sells a managed platform and a larger model (Chandra).

license.name: AI Pubs Open RAIL-M (modified); code Apache-2.0
license.notes: LICENSE read. Weights: free for research, personal use and startups; use is barred for any purpose if you (or your employer/affiliates) had more than 5M USD gross revenue in the prior year or raised more than 5M USD in funding (personal/research use excepted), or if you offer a product competing with the licensor. Share-a-Like clause applies the licence to the model, derivatives and outputs; use-based restrictions must be passed on; hosting as a service counts as distribution; broader commercial licences are sold by the vendor. Verdict policy (README, 2026-11-19): this licence term does not lower tona_fit; kept here for an installer label.

architecture.kind: vision-language, Qwen3.5-style hybrid (18 linear-attention plus 6 full-attention layers, 24 layers), 12-layer vision tower
architecture.attention: linear attention with a full-attention layer every 4th layer
architecture.why_this_design: not stated beyond one VLM handling layout, OCR and tables so one server replaces several models; text-line detection stays a separate small torch model (card Training section)

variants.notes: no official GGUF repo found; the card documents a script that builds GGUF plus mmproj for llama.cpp and an MLX conversion

pc-12gb.notes: 1.5 GB against a VRAM budget of 9.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

pc-16gb.notes: 1.5 GB against a VRAM budget of 13.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

pc-24gb.notes: 1.5 GB against a VRAM budget of 21.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

pc-32gb.notes: 1.5 GB against a VRAM budget of 29.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

mac-16-24gb.notes: 1.5 GB against a GPU share of about 12 GB (KV cache not included)

mac-32gb.notes: 1.5 GB against a GPU share of about 22 GB (KV cache not included)

mac-64gb+.notes: 1.5 GB against a GPU share of about 52 GB (KV cache not included)

engine_support.notes: The surya package auto-spawns vLLM or llama-server; the card says llama.cpp serves it on CPU and Apple Silicon. Surya 2.5 gives no row/column geometry for tables (Surya 2 checkpoint needed).

benchmarks.name: OmniParseBench headline (mean of text, table, layout)
throughput M4 Max (36 GB) llama.cpp Metal, 96 DPI, 8 parallel

strengths: layout labels, reading order and tables from one 0.7B model
writes about a third as many tokens per page as Surya 2 (vendor measurement)
weaknesses: not meant for photos or natural scenes (card Limitations)
old scans and old math are its weakest olmOCR-bench slices (44.3 and 78.6)
best_for: scanned and born-digital pages to HTML/Markdown with layout
avoid_for: commercial use above the revenue/funding thresholds without a licence from the vendor
soft.maturity: third generation of the Surya line; 130k downloads of the repo in the first month

tona_fit.reason: 0.7B, strong self-reported parsing and layout, runs through llama.cpp, fits every class. Benchmarks are all vendor-made on its own OmniParseBench, so compare on our own German documents.
blockers: no Tona module for the Qwen3.5-style OCR model plus layout JSON mode

open_questions: independent scores (OmniParseBench is the vendor's own benchmark)
German page quality (per-language table exists in the card but only for the vendor's internal set)
whether the Share-a-Like clause also binds outputs of users
